news.contents: Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught six passes for 118 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets in Monday night's 34-17 home loss to the Chicago Bears. Smith-Njigba shone again despite quarterback Sam Darnold struggling to a 50% completion rate against a new-look Bears defense. It's the seventh time in 2026 that the fourth-year pro has surpassed 100 receiving yards, and his sixth outing with 11 or more targets. news.analysis: Odunze looked good on Monday night. He led the team with 87 yards on four catches, although he wasn't able to get into the end zone at all, which left him with a limited fantasy total. He will likely have some boom games here and there moving forward, but it remains difficult to trust starting him on an every-week basis at this point.

news.analysis: Strange had the longest gain of his career Sunday, as he went 46 yards on QB Trevor Lawrence's first pass of the game. Lawrence only completed 10 passes in this contest, so Strange and the rest of the Jaguars route runners didn't deliver huge production for fantasy managers. In fact, Strange was one of three Jaguars to tie for the team lead in receptions. He also tied running back Bhayshul Tuten for the team lead in receiving yards. Strange is having a solid season, but the Jaguars run a largely balanced attack, with Lawrence spreading the ball around to a variety of targets.
